best_parts: node p1_t4 and p3_t12: feedback names the tempting model ('feels safe', 'the sign is doing the work') before the refutation, and a sure_note ties the confident error to the old key
node p3: one probe carries three traps (T4d, M1) plus the key, so the learner must place T, N and M in one stem
node p1_h and p4_h: hints point at the question to ask, not the answer
flaws: nodes p2, p4, p5, p7, p8, p9, p10, p11, p12: most probes are two-option (one trap, one key) or a 50/50, so the key is guessable and the path says little about which wrong model the learner holds
whole segment: no which-is-NOT probe and no 'Explain it to me' or fast-lane node, so a learner who misses gets only retry and no second explanation (R5, R6)
node p1: each trap appears once in S7 (TR4 on p1 only), so recovery cannot be credited inside this segment as the trap-map asks for a second form

best_parts: node key: a single three-trap recognition probe (TR4, TR1, correct breast) with the old-year framing, so the old keys are tested together in one stem
nodes key and core: TR1 is tested in two forms (old-key recognition, then the receptor-status vignette), which is the in-segment re-test the trap-map asks for
node gene: a three-option BRCA probe (TR8 swap, TR9 male-cancer error, correct) with an arm-based stem that separates the two genes
flaws: whole segment: no explain or agency node and no fast lane, so the path gives a 1 a.m. learner one route after any miss (R5)
nodes super, halsted, pect, her, drug, tam, lcis, ilc, nipple: two-option probes, so the key is guessable and the trap-map partials are absent (R2, R9)
nodes ilc_hint, halsted_hint and similar: nearly every feedback opens 'Ask which...', so the voice becomes formulaic (R8)

best_parts: node p5, p11, p14: 'which is NOT correct' probes that test BRCA, trastuzumab and LCIS in the exam form, with a true-looking trap whose feedback says why it is true and that the stem asks for the other one

node p8_t and p9_t: feedback names the tempting model ('the sign sounds inflammatory', 'the pectoralis sits right beside the tumour') and an agency 'Explain it to me' gives a second explanation with a different framing
node p13 (tamoxifen bleeding): the vignette makes the trap a clinical decision (reassure versus sample), and the correct reply is the action, not a fact
flaws: node p8 and p9: partial 'T4a' (no chest-wall finding on the sheet) and 'T2' for a 1.8 cm tumour are dominated, since a tired student eliminates them at once (DP2)
node p10: partial 'Halsted spares the axilla' is obviously false, so the probe is a two-real-choice item (DP2)
node p14: the NOT-keyed answer (mastectomy) is the only surgical option, so the key is partly findable by form (DP1)

merge_ideas: c's agency and explain nodes after each trap, with a's sure_note wording, so each confident error gets a sure_note and a second explanation
b's three-trap key probe placed first (TR4, TR1, correct) as the segment entry, to replace a's two-option opener and to give a fast lane for experts

c's NOT probes kept, with c's dominated partials (T4a, Halsted spares axilla) replaced by the trap-map partials (for example 'Excision of the whole lump' or 'Intraductal papilloma is benign, observe all')
b's second-form re-test of TR1 (receptor vignette after the old-key recognition) added to c, so each trap in this segment recurs in a new form
